# Product Line Optimization Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Product Line Optimization Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 23 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved plant environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded line records, proposed Dynamics 365 ERP, Azure IoT Hub and Power BI access and the intended channel; document blocked paths rather than bypass them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger; record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the ERP, telemetry and reporting connections with dedicated, verified references. No customer connection is needed for the synthetic workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare plant manager, production engineer, operations director and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer. | Customer or partner |
| Plant rule ownership | Have the plant owner approve real thresholds, formulas, shift rules and cost assumptions before they replace the packaged synthetic records and calculation rules. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Plant operations owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Line performance, bottleneck review and shift constraints as the plant reviews them manually today. Agree the starting operating picture before judging whether analysis changes bottleneck response or shift planning.

Fill your baseline record:

| Line | Measurement period | Operating score | Constraining station | Leading defect category | Shift constraint | Review owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree plant replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Plant operations owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Plant operations owner | Approve line data sources, audience and success measures; keep synthetic gains, costs and projections out of customer results. |
| Plant leaders and production engineers | Review line, station, option and shift recommendations before any operational decision; retain maintenance, investment and staffing authority. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent in Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before approving any plant connection. |
| ERP, telemetry and reporting connection owners | Approve Dynamics 365 ERP, Azure IoT Hub and Power BI access through dedicated, verified connection references; own connection failures. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check PLO-01 through PLO-04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject forbidden wording, missing identifiers and reshoot-required captures. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route operational decisions back to plant leaders. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Plant replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures have named agreement.
- [ ] The plant owner records current line performance, bottleneck review and shift constraints before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/product-line-optimization/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The administrator's data policies cover the proposed ERP, telemetry and reporting connectors, knowledge sources and intended channel; blocked routes stay blocked.
- [ ] The customer confirms authenticated audience and least-privilege access for plant production data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Plant leaders and production engineers

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Plant leaders and production engineers

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/product-line-optimization/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/product-line-optimization/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/product-line-optimization/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/product-line-optimization/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Product Line Manual Build
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction changes
5. Remove default web search
6. Open the knowledge uploader
7. Upload synthetic production records
8. Upload production optimization rules
9. Verify both knowledge sources
10. Open the SKILL.md uploader
11. Add plant-wide operating health
12. Add constraining-station identification
13. Add improvement-option comparison
14. Add day-swing-night planning
15. Open the model picker
16. Select Claude Sonnet 4.6
17. Audit four skills, two knowledge files, and no web search
18. Open a fresh Preview conversation
19. Pass PLO-01 line health
20. Pass PLO-02 bottlenecks
21. Pass PLO-03 improvement options
22. Pass PLO-04 shift planning
23. Verify Draft and do not publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: PLO-01, PLO-02, PLO-03, PLO-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `ProductionLineOptimizationAgent` and returns `Polymer Molding Line C` and `Electronics Assembly Line A`.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged PLO prompt passes once in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges every case on its final response; annotated screenshots are checkpoints, not the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing plant production, quality or staffing data. Request only the read scopes needed for approved ERP, telemetry and reporting sources. Restrict the audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 ERP

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** ERP, telemetry and reporting connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 ERP — read:** Add approved read-only ERP connector actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 ERP:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 ERP:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 ERP:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Change no staffing or schedule; show the shift plan as a synthetic projection to evaluate. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return analysis and a suggested next step; operational decisions stay with plant leaders.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Azure IoT Hub through an approved connector, workflow, or API

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** ERP, telemetry and reporting connection owners

1. **Bind Azure IoT Hub through an approved connector, workflow, or API — read:** Expose telemetry read-only through an approved connector, MCP server or workflow.

2. **Identity for Azure IoT Hub through an approved connector, workflow, or API:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Azure IoT Hub through an approved connector, workflow, or API:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Azure IoT Hub through an approved connector, workflow, or API:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not recalculate from another source; use only the packaged station figures. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a live reading, system update or equipment action succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Power BI

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** ERP, telemetry and reporting connection owners

1. **Bind Power BI — read-write:** Query approved datasets read-only first; gate any row, refresh or goal update behind approval.

2. **Identity for Power BI:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Power BI:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Power BI:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Say the line is not in the pilot and list the three known lines; invent no figures. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Say what is missing and list the known records; never substitute or calculate a new scenario.

### Step 3-4. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** ERP, telemetry and reporting connection owners

Create dedicated, verified connection references for the approved ERP, telemetry and reporting systems.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Each approved connection preserves the reviewed input and output contract; no live reading or update is claimed without tool evidence.
- [ ] ERP, telemetry and reporting connections use dedicated and verified connection references.
- [ ] No bound tool can start, stop, reconfigure or reschedule equipment or shifts, dispatch maintenance or change staffing.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as intended plant users and an unshared identity; a maker's access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic scores, gains and costs are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked production corpus | All four cases, PLO-01 through PLO-04, include every required marker and none of the forbidden wording. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Operational authority boundary | Any line, station or shift change, maintenance dispatch, investment or headcount commitment is no-go. |
| Quality tradeoff visibility | Every throughput recommendation keeps its quality or defect impact visible; hiding it is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a visible positive anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required captures. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Plant operations owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Plant operations owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved plant audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Plant operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Plant operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Step 6-5. Operate

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review failed plant sessions, hidden-tradeoff or invented-record answers, connection errors and credit consumption in Monitor.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
